newsitem.title: GREECE: Russia, Greece launch Balkan stability initiative.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Greece launch Balkan stability initiative.

text.p: Russia and Greece launched an initiative on Tuesday calling for an expanded Balkan meeting to discuss stability and co-operation in the volatile region.

The proposal, which opens the way for Russia's formal involvement in southeastern Europe, also calls for the participation of the United Nations, the permanent members of the U.N. Security Council, the European Union and other international groups.
Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and Deputy Foreign Minister Nikolay Afanassievsky announced the initiative at a Balkan Foreign Ministers' meeting in this northern Greek city.
"Russia and Greece support the convening, in the first semester of 1998, of meetings of Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Energy, Transport and Communication," Pangalos told a news conference.
As a first step, experts will hold a working session in the fall of 1997 to prepare a planned summit meeting, he said.
"I hope the summit meeting can take place before the end of 1988," Afanassievsky told the news conference.

Russia, which has observer status at the two-day Salonika meeting ending on Tuesday, is involved in trans-Balkan infrastructure projects such as a planned oil pipeline expected to carry Russian crude to the Greek port of Alexandroupolis.
Officials from Albania, Bulgaria, the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, Greece, Romania, Turkey and Serbia are meeting to boost political and economic cooperation in the region.
